data.title: ESB and Tesco Ireland plot 200 kW EV chargers at five stores
data.description: ESB and Tesco Ireland have agreed a new partnership to expand public EV charging at Tesco stores across the country. The first phase will see fast and ultra-fast chargers rated up to 200 kW installed at five Tesco sites in Clarehall, Clearwater, Drogheda, Dundalk and Maynooth.

data.title: Renault Twingo E-Tech: UK pricing revealed
data.description: Renault has confirmed UK pricing for the new all-electric Twingo E-Tech, with the small city car starting at £14,745 once the full £3,750 Electric Car Grant (ECG) is applied. Orders will open in the first quarter of 2027, with customer deliveries expected by March.

data.title: Envoy and LACI launch EV car-sharing initiative in New Jersey
data.description: The partners will deploy up to 30 shared EVs in Hudson and Bergen counties. An $8.5 million (around €7.8 million) state grant funds the project to expand electric mobility in underserved communities.

data.title: India: Energy In Motion secures order for 500 electric heavy-duty trucks
data.description: Indian electric trucking solutions provider Energy In Motion (EIM), an associate company of Ravindra Energy, has bagged a major order for 500 heavy-duty trucks from Sorigin Green Mobility, a homegrown electric truck fleet operator. The duo have signed a memorandum of understanding to deploy these trucks over a period of two years.

data.title: Mother nature strikes.
data.description:
A Tesla driver was alarmed when his Model S ask him to immediately take over from the Autopilot, saying there was a problem with the radar. When he stopped to check, the driver found a moth had given its life to tamper with the sensor. After a quick clean of the radar opening, cruising was back on.

data.title: Tesla Easter Egg.
data.description:
Another one of this small and playful surprises has been discovered in the Model S. This time it is more hands on than previous digital goodies. The charge port will illuminate in all colours of the rainbow when a button on top of the plug is pushed ten times while plugged in. Anyone have disco fever?

data.title: Zenobē expands into Germany
data.description: British commercial fleet electrification specialist Zenobē is bringing its offerings to Germany. Zenobē provides fleet operators with a fixed-price solution that includes EVs, charging infrastructure, battery management, and fleet management software.

data.title: Aptera completes first customer vehicle
data.description: California-based solar electric vehicle developer Aptera has completed its first vehicle destined for a customer. The three-wheeled solar car is set to be delivered to an early investor outside the US.

data.title: Volkswagen ID. Cross opens for UK orders from £26,985
data.description: Volkswagen has opened UK order books for its new all-electric ID. Cross, with prices starting at £26,985. However, entry-level versions will not be available to order until January 2027, meaning customers currently have a choice of two models with the larger battery.

data.title: Onsemi introduces new SiC Platform: EliteSiC M4
data.description: US semiconductor manufacturer Onsemi has introduced the fourth generation of its silicon carbide technology with EliteSiC M4. The new platform is set to increase power density by up to 30 per cent and reduce losses by up to 35 per cent. This could benefit, among other things, the drivetrain systems of electric vehicles.

data.title: Ford Trucks partners with Circulor for battery passport
data.description: Ford is working with technology company Circulor to prepare the its electric truck batteries for the requirements of the European Battery Passport. The focus is on the traceability of battery materials and the collection of supply chain data.

data.title: Hongqi EHS4: a battery-electric SUV with Leapmotor technology for Europe
data.description: Chinese automaker Hongqi is introducing a new eSUV to Europe. The FAW-owned brand will first launch the EHS4 in Italy with a base starting price of €35,900. However, this will be lowered to €32,900 during an initial promotional period.

data.title: Alpitronic builds DC fast charger factory in South Carolina, USA
data.description: Alpitronic is expanding its presence in the USA and investing nearly US$34 million in its own production facility for fast-charging stations in South Carolina. Additionally, the South Tyrolean charging infrastructure specialist is strengthening its North America management with Christopher Balcom as the new Chief Commercial Officer.

data.title: ‘Nova’: Moment Energy launches second-life battery storage system
data.description: Canadian battery technology firm Moment Energy has unveiled Nova, a new battery energy storage system (BESS) built using repurposed EV batteries. The system is now in production at the company's Megafactory 1, with orders open and initial deliveries planned for Q1 2027.

data.title: Tesla opens its first public Megacharger in Texas
data.description: The new Megacharger is the first opened by Tesla in Texas, and adds eight high-powered charging stalls capable of delivering up to 1.2 MW each. The site is located in Mesquite, east of Dallas, and extends the company's public truck charging network into one of the largest freight markets in the US.

data.title: TotalEnergies to install 1,500 EV charging points in London
data.description: TotalEnergies has been selected to install over 1,500 new public EV charging points in the London Borough of Tower Hamlets over the next four years. This project marks the first charging contract in London to receive funding from the Government's LEVI scheme.

data.title: Compact premium: first drive in the new Audi A2 e-tron
data.description: With the A2 e-tron, Audi is introducing a compact car to the market that doesn’t neatly fit into any of the classic categories. In Audi’s internal logic, it is set to replace both the A1 and the Q2. For Volkswagen, it is another MEB derivative. For the general public, it is primarily the successor to the cult classic original A2 from 1999. We took a close look at the compact premium speedster for a day, testing both the 125 kW entry-level model and the 240 kW top version.

data.title: Tesla plant manager André Thierig faces penalty order following dispute with IG Metall
data.description: The Fürstenwalde/Spree district court has issued a penalty order against André Thierig, head of Tesla Gigafactory Berlin-Brandenburg, for defamation. Thierig had claimed in February that a works council meeting had been illegally recorded, a claim the IG Metall union denies. Thierig has already filed an objection against the penalty order.

data.title: Envision AESC surpasses production volume milestone for 46120 battery cells
data.description: Envision AESC states that it has now delivered over 10 million units of its cylindrical 46120 battery cells. Series production at the Chinese plants in Jiangsu and Hebei began in July 2026. The BMW iX5 has been confirmed as the first model to use these cells.

data.title: Sila secures billion-dollar offtake agreement with Panasonic
data.description: US battery material manufacturer Sila will supply Panasonic Energy with its silicon-carbon anode material, Titan Silicon, in the future. The multi-year agreement could reach a volume of over one billion US dollars.
